warningContent.para: Flight-critical indication systems must be operational before takeoff. Operating aircraft with inoperative flight instruments may result in spatial disorientation, loss of situational awareness, and catastrophic failure.
Verify all primary flight displays, standby instruments, and backup systems are functional before flight.
Do not operate aircraft with inoperative flight data recorders (FDR) or cockpit voice recorders (CVR) unless authorized by regulatory authority and MEL.
Recording systems are required for accident investigation and safety analysis. Failure to maintain these systems may violate regulatory requirements.
Master caution and warning systems must annunciate properly. Failure to respond to caution/warning indications may result in system failure, fire, structural damage, or loss of aircraft.
Test all caution and warning lights during preflight inspection. Any malfunctions must be corrected before flight.

Ensure display brightness is adjusted appropriately for ambient lighting conditions. Displays set too dim may be unreadable in bright sunlight. Displays set too bright may cause crew discomfort and fatigue.
Adjust display brightness before takeoff and as needed during flight operations.
Do not disable or override alert priority systems without proper authorization. The alert priority system ensures critical warnings are presented to crew in the correct order.
Improper alert prioritization may result in crew missing critical system failures.
